verdict_reason: Re-derived from Hosseini & Fedorenko 2023 and checked against the authors' own code: the angle kernel (diff -> row-normalise -> dot -> arccos) matches the official curvature_utils.py to max 1.33e-15 over 200 random trajectories, and the layer statistic is the paper's mean-of-per-sentence-means (compute_model_curvature: all_layer_curve.append([np.mean(x) for x in curvature])). The task also reproduces the paper's published random-trajectory anchor: Fig. S6 states the distribution 'peaks at ~120 degrees (119.99)' for 8408 Gaussian trajectories of dimension 1600 and length 6-19; BLME returns 119.9985 deg against the analytic arccos(-1/2) = 120.0000 deg, rel 1.1e-4 vs the published value.
comparable_reason: The headline curvatures are NOT size proxies: over 61 models curvature_mean_last_layer has Spearman -0.004 with d_model and +0.084 with n_layers, straightening_ratio -0.063 / -0.095, curvature_overall_mean -0.190 / -0.205. The real cross-model hazard is the tokenizer, not scale: curvature_overall_mean has Spearman -0.634 with log(vocab) (q25 -0.626, mid-layer -0.505). The mechanism is protocol, not geometry -- the shared cache truncates every model at 512 TOKENS, so a 262k-vocab tokenizer's 512-token trajectory covers substantially more text than a 32k-vocab one, and the models are therefore not compared on the same linguistic content. curvature_slope retains +0.373 with log(params) after depth normalisation.
normalized_variant: curvature_slope (OLS of per-layer curvature on NORMALIZED depth l/(n_layers-1))
normalized_ok_detail: MEASURED, and it works. Reconstructing the un-normalized slope (raw layer index) as slope_norm/(L-1) over the same 61 models: Spearman with n_layers falls from +0.845 (raw) to +0.257 (shipped normalized), with d_model from +0.763 to +0.349, with log(params) from +0.821 to +0.373. The depth divisor removes about 70% of the depth association it targets. The residual +0.26 with n_layers is small enough to be signal rather than construction. The task also correctly keeps n_layers behind a _meta_ prefix so it cannot enter the feature matrix as a depth counter.
github_reason: Fetched sent_sampling/utils/curvature_utils.py and straightening/compute_curvature_and_surprisal_for_GPTModel.py from the authors' repo and EXECUTED the official normalized/diff/dot/arccos kernel against BLME's _trajectory_angles on 200 random (T,D) trajectories: max absolute angle difference 1.33e-15. The official pipeline confirms two BLME choices: (a) curve_change is baselined at curve_[1], i.e. the first BLOCK output, which is exactly BLME's layer 0 after the cache drops hs[0]; (b) the layer value is the mean of per-sentence means, not a pooled angle average. It also shows two BLME departures: the official code tokenizes with tokenizer.tokenize + convert_tokens_to_ids (no special tokens) and uses ALL tokens (no skip_first).
paper_reason: Two independent published readouts reproduce. (1) Fig. S6A: 'The distribution peaks at ~120 degrees (119.99)' for n=8408 random trajectories in 1600 dimensions of length 6-19. Same-protocol simulation through BLME's kernel: 119.9985 deg (skip_first=0) and 119.9970 deg (skip_first=1) -- rel 1.1e-4 and 9.7e-5 vs 119.99, and the analytic value is exactly arccos(-1/2) = 120 deg since E<v_t,v_t+1> = -d*sigma^2 and E||v||^2 = 2*d*sigma^2. (2) Fig. S6B shows GPT2-XL starting at ~120 deg at the input layer; the shipped run for gpt2-1.5b reports curvature_mean_first_layer = 120.537 deg, rel 0.45%. (The paper's GPT2-XL minimum is ~105-107 deg vs BLME's 113.65 -- that gap is the corpus, UD sentences of 6-19 words vs 512-token WikiText passages.)
confounds_reason: Not a size proxy (see comparable: |Spearman| <= 0.35 with d_model / n_layers / log(params) for every headline scalar except the slope). It IS associated with the tokenizer: curvature_overall_mean Spearman -0.634 with log(vocab) over 61 models. Because the correlation runs through the fixed 512-token truncation rather than through model width or depth, I record this as SUSPECTED (protocol-mediated) rather than CONFIRMED architectural confounding.
defects: defaults.yaml sets skip_first_tokens: 1 with the comment 'drop BOS', but 10 of the 16 tokenizer families I tested prepend NO special token (gpt2, distilgpt2, pythia, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, SmolLM2, OLMo, phi-1_5, Yi ...), so for those models the task discards a real content state, while for the 6 that do prepend one (OPT, Llama-3.2, Gemma, Gemma-2, TinyLlama, Mistral) it correctly removes BOS. The protocol is therefore not the same across the zoo. MEASURED IMPACT under the shipped 100-passage WikiText protocol is small: |d straightening_ratio| 0.00008-0.00083 (0.17%-1.89% relative), |d curvature_overall_mean| 0.19-0.33 deg, and the minimum-curvature layer is unchanged in 6/6 models. This REFUTES codex's stated magnitudes ('up to 33.5%', 'moved GPT-2's minimum-curvature layer from 8 to 11'), which came from an 80-short-sentence corpus where token 0 is a large fraction of the trajectory.

The cache truncates at a fixed 512 TOKENS, not a fixed amount of text, so models with different tokenizers are measured on different linguistic content. This is the likely mechanism behind Spearman -0.634 between curvature_overall_mean and log(vocab) across 61 models.

The paper's defining quantity, the per-layer curvature CHANGE Delta C_l = C_l - C_0 and the layer of maximum drop, is not emitted; straightening_ratio and curvature_slope are BLME summaries. For a profile whose minimum sits mid-network (gpt2: min at layer 8 of 12, last layer higher than mid), straightening_ratio understates the drop the paper reports -- BLME gpt2 mid 114.73 vs last 114.64.

The shipped corpus (100 WikiText passages, 512 tokens) is not the paper's UDsubset8408 (8408 sentences of 6-19 words), so the published GPT2-XL layer curve is reproducible only in its layer-0 value and direction, not in its depth.
fix: Set skip_first_tokens: 0 in defaults.yaml and instead strip an ACTUALLY PRESENT leading special token by inspecting input_ids against tokenizer.all_special_ids, so BOS-prepending and non-prepending tokenizers get the same treatment. Emit the paper's per-layer Delta C_l profile plus min_delta_curvature and its normalized argmin depth alongside the existing BLME summaries. Consider a fixed-character (or fixed-word) truncation instead of fixed-token so the log(vocab) association can be tested rather than assumed. No change is needed to the kernel, the layer aggregation, or the slope normalisation -- all three verified.
